# Get the tar file ready. The archive holds a directory, two regular files,
# a symbolic link and a hard link. Modification times are not checked since
# their rendering depends on the local time zone.
base64 tar.base64 test.tar

mito -use file,mime,try src.cel
! stderr .
cmp stdout want.txt

-- src.cel --
{
	"direct": file('test.tar', 'application/x-tar').File.map(f, [f.Name, f.Type, f.Linkname, f.IsDir, f.Size, f.Mode, string(f.Data)]),
	"buffered_same": file('test.tar', 'application/x-tar').File.map(f, [f.Name, f.Type, f.Linkname, f.IsDir, f.Size, f.Mode, string(f.Data)]) ==
		file('test.tar').mime('application/x-tar').File.map(f, [f.Name, f.Type, f.Linkname, f.IsDir, f.Size, f.Mode, string(f.Data)]),
	"invalid": try(b"this is not a tar archive".mime('application/x-tar')),
}
-- tar.base64 --

-- want.txt --
{
	"buffered_same": true,
	"direct": [
		[
			"dir/",
			"5",
			"",
			true,
			0,
			509,
			""
		],
		[
			"dir/a.txt",
			"0",
			"",
			false,
			4,
			436,
			"one\n"
		],
		[
			"link",
			"2",
			"dir/a.txt",
			false,
			0,
			511,
			""
		],
		[
			"b.txt",
			"0",
			"",
			false,
			4,
			436,
			"two\n"
		],
		[
			"hard",
			"1",
			"b.txt",
			false,
			0,
			436,
			""
		]
	],
	"invalid": "tar: unexpected EOF"
}
